reasoning_content:
The user is planning a long weekend in Montreal in late October with two friends on a modest budget. They want recommendations for what to see, where to eat, and how to get around.

Let me think about what I actually know about Montreal and can provide genuinely useful information.

Montreal is a Canadian city in Quebec. Key facts:
- It's the largest city in Quebec, a French-speaking province
- Late October is autumn - the fall foliage is usually at or near peak in late October, which is a highlight
- The weather in late October is cool, typically 5-15°C (40s-50s°F), can be rainy

Neighborhoods and attractions:
- Old Montreal (Vieille-Montréal) - cobblestone streets, Old Port (Vieux-Port), Notre-Dame Basilica (basilique Notre-Dame) - absolutely stunning Gothic Revival interior, free to enter the nave
- Old Port - has activities, views
- Old Lachine Canal (Canal de Lachine) - great for walking/cycling, beautiful fall foliage
- Mount Royal (Mont-Royal) - park designed by Frederick Law Olmsted, the overlook (Belvédère du Mont-Royal) has great city views, the cross at the top
- Plateau Mont-Royal - colorful houses with staircases (escaliers extérieurs), murals, trendy cafes
- Mile End - hipster area, bagels!
- Little Italy (Petite-Italie)
- Westmount - upscale
- Old Port area
- Jean-Talon Market (Marché Jean-Talon) - one of the largest outdoor markets in North America, great for food
- Atwater Market
- Old Lachine Canal

Food - Montreal specialties:
- Bagels - St-Vincent bagels (Saint-Vincent) in Mile End are famous, very different from NY bagels, made with honey and in wood-fired ovens. Also Fairmount Bagels in the Mile End.
- Smoked meat - Schwartz's Deli (Schwartz's) on Saint-Laurent is iconic, famous smoked meat sandwich
- Poutine - frites, cheese curds, gravy. Le Duplex, La Banquise (open 24 hours), etc.
- Bagel and smoked meat are the big ones
- Crepes
- Bagel
- Tourtière (meat pie) - seasonal
- Maple syrup products
